system_prompt:
You are an expert Toptal PMO Delivery Lead and Startup Specialist.
Your goal is to extract structured project management data from provided project documents, pre-sales decks, and context notes to build the PMO Startup Kit.

STRICT BUSINESS RULES & CONSTRAINTS:
1. NO HALLUCINATION: Extract only factual information present in the input documents.
2. NO SOW OR EXTERNAL DOCUMENT REFERENCES: The consumers of this report DO NOT have access to the Statement of Work (SOW), pre-sales decks, contracts, or source documents. Do NOT reference 'the SOW', 'Statement of Work', 'input documents', 'source documents', 'page numbers', or 'clause numbers' in any extracted text, descriptions, questions, deliverables, milestones, risks, or assumptions. All text must be completely self-contained and document-agnostic.
3. CONCISE & SIMPLIFIED: Keep all field values, summaries, and descriptions short, clear, direct, and concise (1-2 sentences maximum). Simplify the report text so that stakeholders can understand the project baseline instantly without legalistic jargon or redundant phrasing.
4. MISSING ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA: If a deliverable's acceptance criteria are not explicitly specified in the text, set acceptance_criteria to null (None).
5. MISSING DATES: If milestone dates are not explicitly stated, set external_date to null (None).
6. SOURCE TRACEABILITY: Every extracted item must include a valid SourceReference with:
   - document_name: exact filename where the information was found
   - clause_or_slide: the section number, heading, or slide number (e.g. "Section 3.2", "Slide 4", "Page 2")
   - confidence_score: floating point score between 0.0 and 1.0 indicating extraction confidence.
7. GOVERNANCE TIERS: Valid tiers are 'Guided', 'Partnered', 'Elevated'. Default to 'Partnered' if not specified.
8. CONTRACT TYPES: Common types include 'Time and Materials' and 'Fixed Bid'.
prompt:
Analyze the deliverables in the provided documents and extract explicit acceptance process details. Keep descriptions concise, direct, and self-contained without referencing the SOW or other documents.

CONSTRAINTS:
1. Focus only on primary deliverables and major acceptance gates (maximum 15 deliverables).
2. Keep all text fields (description, acceptance criteria, evidence, rework path) brief and direct (1-2 sentences maximum).
3. Do NOT cite or reference the SOW, contracts, or source documents in descriptions or criteria.

For each deliverable:
- id: Deliverable ID (DEL-01, etc.)
- name: Deliverable title
- description: Concise deliverable description (1-2 sentences)
- sow_reference: Section or clause reference
- acceptance_criteria: Explicit criteria or null (do not cite documents)
- evidence_required: Documents, artifacts, or sign-offs required as proof (1-2 sentences)
- client_approver: Named client approver or role, or '[UNASSIGNED - TO BE CONFIRMED]'
- submission_target_date: Target submission date (YYYY-MM-DD) if stated
- review_window: Client review window (e.g. '5 business days')
- rejection_rework_path: Rework and resubmission mechanism (1-2 sentences)

EXHIBIT A
ARC Genomics Platform - Implementation Specifications
This Exhibit A is incorporated by reference into the Statement of Work to which it is attached (the
"SOW") and forms part of the Scope of Work performed thereunder. Capitalized terms used
herein and not otherwise defined have the meanings given to them in the SOW or the Agreement
referenced therein. In the event of any conflict between this Exhibit and the terms of the SOW,
the terms of the SOW will control unless expressly stated otherwise.
1.​ OVERVIEW
Under this Exhibit A, Toptal will build part of the ARC application and deliver the quality assurance
(QA) test automation for the ARC program across four sequential Milestones: P1 Foundation, P2a
Services and Data, P2b Application Surface, and P3 Launch. ARC is one application within a
larger Client platform. Client owns the platform layer (including Terraform and infrastructure) and
the data tier (including the ingestion pipelines and the Snowflake data model); Toptal owns ARC
application development, comprising the micro-frontend shell, the ARC micro-frontend, the
FastAPI services, and the nomenclature service. Toptal will also write and execute the automated
test scripts as defined in this Exhibit. Each Milestone is an acceptance gate with its own Work
Output, Acceptance Criteria, and Sign-Off, and user acceptance testing (UAT) runs after each
Milestone. Story references (e.g., HS-4762) identify the corresponding items in Client's estimation
sheet.
Toptal will perform the Work in this phase using methodology and terminology aligned with the
Scaled Agile Framework (SAFe). Unless otherwise expressly defined in this Exhibit A or the SOW,
agile and product-development terms used herein (e.g., "epic," "feature," "user story," "MVP,"
"backlog") have the meanings given by SAFe (scaledagileframework.com). For terms not
addressed by SAFe, industry-standard definitions apply.
2.​ ACTIVITIES
Toptal will perform the following Work organized into the following phases, aligned to the
Milestones in Section 4. Bullets describe the nature of the Work performed in each phase;
specific Work Output and Acceptance Criteria are defined in Section 4.
2.1.​ P1 Foundation
●​ Build the micro-frontend shell, including global navigation, application routing,
and remote mounting for future genomics applications, adopting Client's
existing design system and making it available to remotes (HS-4762).
●​ Integrate the Azure AD / MSAL authentication flow into the shell and
propagate it to remotes (HS-4763).
●​ Build and execute an end-to-end test harness covering shell composition,
navigation, and authentication flows (HS-4765).
●​ Build automated pipeline quality gates and deployment smoke checks
(HS-4770).
●​ Perform negative and abuse-case authentication testing and security scanning
(HS-4938).
●​ Validate referential integrity and query patterns of the Client-built Snowflake

--- Page 2 ---
data model (HS-4782).
●​ Validate Client-built data governance controls and audit classification
coverage (HS-4941).
2.2.​ P2a Services and Data
●​ Implement FastAPI faceted search, filter, and detail endpoints over the
Snowflake ARC tables (HS-4777).
●​ Implement asynchronous processing for long-running queries, including a task
queue (Celery/RQ) and health checks (HS-4778).
●​ Perform backend integration testing against the Snowflake development
environment and load testing against the sub-second search SLA (HS-4779).
●​ Perform a performance engineering spike covering benchmarking, query
observability, p95 latency definitions, and a tuning backlog (HS-4942).
●​ Build the OneGWAS direct-write integration that writes completed OneGWAS
results (variant and PHG/GATSBY) to Snowflake ARC with retryable error
handling (HS-4803), and execute end-to-end and failure/retry tests (HS-4804).
●​ Validate Client-built data ingestion and migration, covering GWAS Atlas ETL
import coverage and schema-change handling (HS-4797), MTA Store migration
data quality including domain-user comparison, a data-quality issue log, and
sign-off support (HS-4785), and PHG/GATSBY haplotype ingestion linkage and
completeness (HS-4807).
●​ Validate PubMed/literature extraction accuracy on key fields with an
end-to-end run (HS-4801), and validate trait taxonomy coverage and approvals
(HS-4791).
2.3.​ P2b Application Surface
●​ Build the ARC micro-frontend faceted search (crop, trait, marker, significance,
source, and haplotype type) with a paginated, sortable results table (HS-4772).
●​ Build the result detail view (markers, trials, haplotypes, and study) and
PHG/GATSBY interval-based visualization (HS-4773).
●​ Build the haplotype-type filter, result indicator, interval-based detail, and
variant-versus-pangenome comparison (HS-4809), and the supporting
haplotype search/filter endpoints (HS-4810).
●​ Implement backend endpoints and data access for haplotype association
results (HS-4813).
●​ Implement the nomenclature service, including trait resolution, synonym
lookup, unmapped-term handling, and ARC backend integration (HS-4793).
●​ Build and execute frontend unit, integration, accessibility, and performance
tests (HS-4775), backend haplotype integration tests (HS-4815), nomenclature
service tests (HS-4794), and haplotype search and visualization tests (HS-4811).
2.4.​ P3 Launch
●​ Build and execute integration, performance, security, and cross-browser
(Chrome and Edge) test suites covering all data flows and UI/API critical paths
in staging at production-like volume (HS-4825).
●​ Provide test data, fixtures, and environment support for integration testing
(HS-4826).

--- Page 3 ---
●​ Execute UAT cycles with Client's scientist groups, and triage and track defects
(HS-4828).
●​ Perform a pre-launch hardening and stabilization iteration after integration
testing and UAT to close critical and high defects before cutover (HS-4943).
●​ Execute production smoke tests and post-deployment validation, including a
48-hour defect watch (HS-4832).
●​ Confirm MTA Store feature parity and zero legacy traffic before decommission
(HS-4788).
●​ Produce training materials and user documentation (HS-4829).
3.​ QUALITY ASSURANCE AND TEST AUTOMATION
Toptal will deliver the QA test automation Work Output listed in Section 4. The following
principles apply to all QA Work under this Exhibit A:
●​ Test scope. Testing ARC means testing against the full platform. Single sign-on (SSO) and
the external integrations are within the test scope.
●​ Form of Work Output. QA Work Output consists of automated test scripts, their
execution, and the resulting defect reports, rather than manual QA passes.
●​ Remediation. Where a test fails against a Client-built component, pipeline, dataset, or
environment, remediation of that failure is Client's responsibility. Toptal's delivery of a test
for a component does not constitute a commitment by Toptal that the component will
meet its target.
●​ Certification Acceptance Criteria. Acceptance Criteria labeled "Certification" in Section 3
apply to components built by Client. For each such criterion, Toptal's Work Output is the
test scripts, their execution, and a defect report measured against the stated target.
Achievement of the target itself is Client's responsibility and is not a condition of
Acceptance of Toptal's Work Output.
●​ Re-testing. Following Client's remediation of a failed Certification target, Toptal will
re-execute the applicable test scripts in accordance with the Assumptions outlined in this
contract. Additional re-runs will be addressed by Change Order.
●​ Test script maintenance. Maintenance of test scripts means in-flight upkeep of Toptal's
test scripts during development. It does not include a post-launch maintenance phase.
●​ For test-suite Work Output (HS-4765, 4775, 4779, 4794, 4804, 4811, 4815, 4825),
Acceptance requires delivery of the scripts, execution in the target environment, and a
results report against the stated targets. Achievement of the targets is assessed under
the corresponding build story, not the test deliverable.
4.​ WORK OUTPUT
Certification Acceptance Criteria. Acceptance Criteria labeled Certification measures a
component built by Client, as described in Section 1.1. For those criteria, Acceptance of Toptal's
Work Output requires delivery and execution of the test scripts and issuance of the defect report;
the stated target is Client's to achieve and remediate. All other Acceptance Criteria measure
Toptal-built Work.
Latency Acceptance Criteria. Latency and render-time Acceptance Criteria measure Toptal-built
components running on Client-owned platform components. These include Snowflake
(warehouse sizing and configuration, schema, views, and data volume), Azure AD, CloudFront,
Client's upstream systems (including OneGWAS), and Client's network and environments.
Telemetry, including the query observability delivered under HS-4942, may show that a missed

--- Page 4 ---
target is attributable to a Client-owned platform component rather than to Toptal-built code or
Toptal-authored queries. In that case, the criterion will be treated as met for Toptal's Work
Output, and the finding will be recorded in the defect report for Client remediation.

5.​ ENGAGEMENT GOVERNANCE
5.1.​ Engagement Cadence
This phase of work will maintain the following cadence:
●​ Kickoff Call (Day 1): full-team alignment session to review phase governance,
confirm cadenced meeting times, and discuss outstanding access provisioning
and documentation (if applicable).
●​ Biweekly Sprint Demo: review work completed in past sprint, review
Milestone status, open risks/issues, and decisions needed from the Client.
●​ Daily Standups: Toptal team will join Client’s daily standups to track progress
and collaborate with the Client-side team members.
●​ Ad-Hoc Working Sessions: scheduled as needed throughout the engagement
to align on open questions that pertain to the delivery of this scope of work.
●​ Milestone Acceptance Review: held at the end of each milestone. Covers
milestone acceptance, Work Output review, and forward-looking risk
assessment for the next milestone.
5.2.​ Weekly Report
The Delivery Manager will send a Weekly Status Report to the designated Client
Contact after the Weekly Status Meeting. The Client Contact will be asked to send
their confirmation of acceptance and/or any additional feedback in response to each
report. The report will cover:
●​ Milestone billing snapshot
●​ Milestone progress
●​ Work Output status for the active Milestone
●​ Open risks & issues
●​ Open blockers & decisions needed
6.​ CLIENT RESPONSIBILITIES
The Client shall provide the following:
●​ All Client code dependencies and Client-owned stories must be completed before the
related Toptal-owned Work can begin.

--- Page 8 ---
●​ Make the following Client personnel available for the Toptal stories that depend on them:
domain users; domain experts for trait taxonomy; scientist UAT groups; and Client's
identity provider (IdP) team for Azure AD / MSAL authentication.
●​ Maintain the development, staging, and production environments and resolve
environment blockers throughout all Milestones, including P2a and P2b.
●​ Remediate defects identified by Toptal's testing in Client-built components, pipelines,
datasets, and environments.
●​ Provide access to the design system (code library, tokens, design files, guidelines and a
named contact), and UI/UX designs for the Milestone 3 screens.
●​ Provide Milestone Sign-Off through Client's designated approvers,
●​ Coding standards and delivery documentation standards (merge request process, code
review gates, unit and integration test requirements) are required on or before the start
date.
●​ Timely written response to decision requests flagged in weekly status reports.
●​ Timely written response to provide confirmation and/or feedback upon receiving each
weekly status report.
7.​ ASSUMPTIONS & DEPENDENCIES
●​ The Milestones run sequentially as acceptance gates. P2a Services and Data begins upon
completion of HS-4781; P2b Application Surface begins upon acceptance of P2a; and P3
Launch begins upon acceptance of P2b.
●​ The Cogen API is assumed to be available and stable at approximately 95%, as assessed
by Syngenta. Test failures and re-test cycles arising from Cogen availability below that
level will be addressed by Change Order.
●​ The estimated schedule, measured from the Start Date, is P1 weeks 1–6, P2a weeks 7–16,
P2b weeks 17–21, and P3 weeks 22–26.
●​ The schedule and cost were created considering that no breaks or stoppages due to
holidays will occur to impact delivery.
●​ UAT runs after each Milestone and is included within the fixed price. UAT is limited to two
(2) runs per Milestone, covering all UAT and not only Toptal-built Work. UAT runs beyond
two will be addressed by Change Order.
●​ Changes outside Toptal's control that require additional UAT or test cycles which result in
rework of Toptal's test scripts will be addressed by Change Order. Such changes include
upstream Snowflake schema changes and API taxonomy shifts.
●​ Client owns the platform layer (including Terraform and infrastructure) and the data tier
(including the ingestion pipelines and the Snowflake data model). The platform shell hosts
CloudFront and Active Directory.
●​ ARC reads Snowflake tables populated by upstream systems (MTA, 1GWAS, GATS-B, and
GWAS Atlas), all of which are within Client's control.
●​ The external API integrations within scope are Cogen and Tagasys.

--- Page 9 ---
●​ Toptal will use Client's existing design system for all user-facing screens. Estimates
include integrating it and building up to [N] ARC-specific components (e.g., interval
visualization, facet panel), and exclude creating, extending or maintaining the design
system. Further components or changes are addressed by Change Order.
●​ By the Start Date, the Client will provide access to the design system (code library, tokens,
design files, guidelines and a named contact), and UI/UX designs for the Milestone 3
screens. The Client will give advance notice of design-system changes; resulting rework
is addressed by Change Order.
●​ Toptal will write and execute the automated test scripts listed as Work Output in Section 4,
covering Toptal-built Work and the Client-built items identified there as Certification.
Testing of other Client-built components, pipelines or environments is not included and
may be added by Change Order.
●​ Toptal's Milestone schedule and fixed fees assume that Client completes the Client-built
work, personnel availability, environment support, reviews, and approvals described in
Section 5 before the dependent Toptal Work is scheduled to begin.
8.​ THIRD PARTY ITEMS
The following Third Party Items are used during the ARC engagement, and the party
providing or making each item available is indicated below. Client's post-delivery license
responsibilities are governed by the Third Party Items section of the SOW.
●​ Snowflake — Data platform hosting the ARC tables that Toptal's services read and write
and against which Toptal's tests execute. Provided by Client during the engagement.
●​ Azure AD / MSAL — Identity provider and authentication library used for shell and remote
authentication. Provided by Client during the engagement.
●​ Azure Key Vault — Secrets management used by the CI/CD pipelines. Provided by Client
during the engagement.
●​ CloudFront — Content delivery hosted by the Client platform shell. Provided by Client
during the engagement.
●​ Cogen and Tagasys APIs — External API integrations within the test scope. Provided by
Client during the engagement. [confirm]
●​ Playwright — Open-source framework for end-to-end testing of the ARC React/Next.js
front end, and for UI and API test automation of the Python services where applicable.
Provided by Client during the engagement.
●​ Jest — Open-source JavaScript test framework for component and integration testing of
the ARC front end, including code coverage reporting. Provided by Client during the
engagement.
●​ React Testing Library — Open-source library used with Jest for component and
integration testing of the ARC front end. Provided by Client during the engagement.
●​ Pytest — Open-source primary test framework for the Python (FastAPI) services, including
the nomenclature service. Provided by Client during the engagement.

--- Page 10 ---
9.​ OUT OF SCOPE
The following are excluded from Toptal's Work under this Exhibit A. Except where noted, each
item is performed by Client. Toptal's QA test automation for these items, where listed in
Section 3, remains in scope.
●​ Platform infrastructure and DevOps, including environment and IaC strategy, Terraform
modules, CI/CD pipelines, monitoring and alerting, and shell telemetry and observability
(HS-4766, HS-4767, HS-4768, HS-4769, HS-4764).
●​ Security design, threat modeling, platform hardening, and RBAC/secrets implementation
(HS-4936, HS-4937).
●​ Architecture and design stories, including the shell architecture and onboarding contract,
ARC frontend component architecture, API design and OpenAPI contract, OneGWAS
output contract, nomenclature service interface design, haplotype search/visualization
design, and backend haplotype support design (HS-4761, HS-4771, HS-4776, HS-4802,
HS-4792, HS-4808, HS-4812).
●​ Snowflake data model design, schema DDL, schema extensions for haplotypes, and data
governance design and controls (HS-4780, HS-4781, HS-4814, HS-4939, HS-4940).
●​ Data ingestion and migration build, including MTA Store migration design and scripts,
GWAS Atlas ETL, PubMed/literature ingestion, PHG/GATSBY haplotype ingestion, and trait
taxonomy definition (HS-4783, HS-4784, HS-4795, HS-4796, HS-4798, HS-4799, HS-4805,
HS-4806, HS-4789, HS-4790).
●​ Integration test plan (HS-4824) and UAT coordination and sign-off (HS-4827).
●​ Go-live planning and operational runbook handover, production deployment, MTA Store
decommission planning, and legacy infrastructure teardown and redirects (HS-4830,
HS-4831, HS-4786, HS-4787).
●​ Hypercare and post-go-live support beyond the 48-hour post-deployment defect watch
(HS-4944), and any post-launch maintenance phase.
●​ Remediation of defects in Client-built components, pipelines, datasets, or environments.
●​ Achievement of numeric targets for Client-built work, including PubMed extraction
precision, GWAS Atlas import coverage, trait taxonomy coverage, Snowflake referential
integrity, CI/CD quality gates, and decommission parity.
●​ Creation, extensions, or maintenance of the Client-provided design system.
